newsitem.title: MEXICO: United Airlines says Mexico traffic still down.
newsitem.headline: United Airlines says Mexico traffic still down.

text.p: Passenger traffic through Mexico City's Benito Juarez International Airport has picked up since the December 1994 peso devaluation, but remains below record levels, Josue Meza, United Airlines' general director in Mexico, said on Thursday.
"Traffic has not returned to 1994 levels, the best year we registered," Meza said. "We've seen a notable recovery and the worst seems to have passed ... more domestic travellers, not just tourists."

Mexicans' disposable income plummeted after the peso was devalued and inflation shot up in 1995's financial crisis. Gradually recovering employment and income levels have led to slow growth in 1996 internal consumption.
United Airlines is a unit of UAL Corp.
